newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL makes big push into Quebec gas business.
newsitem.headline: IPL makes big push into Quebec gas business.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc made a major push into Quebec's natural gas business on Tuesday by buying a big stake in Quebec holding company Noverco Inc and offering a large chunk of its own stock to Noverco.

Under the deal, IPL will join government-owned electric utility Hydro-Quebec and Gaz de France as Noverco owners, participating in gas pipeline and distribution operation and development in Quebec and Canada's Maritime provinces.
IPL said it would acquire 32 percent of Noverco -- whose main asset is an 80 percent stake in gas distribution concern
In a related deal, IPL would issue to Noverco 6 million shares, or 8 percent, of its common stock for proceeds of C$287 million. The shares were priced at C$47.85 each.

Calgary-based IPL, which operates Canada's main oil pipeline system and owns Toronto-based gas utility Consumers Gas Co, also said it would sell to Noverco for C$750,000 an option to buy 1.5 million more shares in mid-1998 at C$51 each.
That would bring Noverco's ownership interest in IPL to 10 percent.

After the deal, Hydro-Quebec will have a 41 percent stake in Noverco, IPL will have 32 percent, Gaz de France 18 percent, Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion eight percent and Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec one percent.
IPL and Hydro-Quebec said the move meant a big boost for both companies into the expanding world of energy providers offering customers both natural gas and electicity in fast-deregulating markets.
For its part, IPL would extract new revenues from the eastern Canadian regions, while in partnership with firms that offer complementary services, IPL Chief Executive Brian MacNeill said.

"In particular, Noverco has high quality gas distribution and pipeline assets which will contribute an immediate boost to earnings per share, plus significant future growth opportunities," MacNeill said in a statement.
The deal follows several recent moves by IPL to expand and diversify energy service operations.

Earlier this year, it announced a retail gas distribution business in Ontario, a joint venture with Nova Scotia Power to pursue gas distribution opportunities in that province, an alliance with Houston-based NGC Corp and oil marketing venture with Gulf Canada Resources Ltd.
"Those are all energy services and a direct result of competition and a changing energy environment in North America," IPL spokesman Byron Neiles said.
Also on Tuesday, Hydro-Quebec Chairman Andre Caille was named as a director of IPL. IPL said it would name three representetives to Noverco's board.
IPL stock was halted throughout Tuesday's trading sessions on the Toronto Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))

In January, Hydro-Quebec bought 40 percent of Noverco, which also owns Northern New England Gas Corp and Vermont Gas Systems Inc, in a C$309 million deal. It bought a further six percent from Gaz de France a month later for C$46.6 million.
The partnership with IPL meant Hydro-Quebec was poised to achieve the utility's much-publicized desire to enter new markets, Hydro-Quebec spokesman Guy Litalien told Reuters.
"It is a step forward for our new strategy which is of being a multi-energy provider. This deal means that Hydro is now a gas wholesaler," Litalien said.
